thread:
olivia: Heads up — after merging the scheduler change (prefer_small_kernels) we see periodic latency cliffs in prod inference that line up with sharp cudaMalloc spikes in the nsys timeline. sample: https://artifacts/redwood/perf/1952/trace-clip.png :eyes:

sam: Ugh. Do we have an nsys capture that includes the host-side alloc stack? We need to see which callsites are triggering cudaMalloc instead of pooled alloc.

miguel: I grabbed a short nsys run from a repro cluster: `nsys profile -o /tmp/1952 -t cuda,osrt,cublas --capture-range c --trace=nvtx ./invoke_test.sh`

jen: Perfetto playback looks similar — lots of tiny kernels interleaved with host-side cudaMallocAsync calls. Timeline snippet:```
Host: cudaMallocAsync -> 3.2ms
GPU : small-kernel-A -> 0.6ms
GPU : small-kernel-B -> 0.9ms
Host: cudaMallocAsync -> 3.1ms
```

olivia: Important detail: the KV cache hotpath is being favored by the new selector, which increases churn of short-lived tensors on the arena boundary. I suspect the arena free lists are not servicing these sizes and fall back to cudaMallocAsync.

derek: That matches what I saw locally. The slab recycler has a hole at 4k-12k sizes. Those get escalated to the slow path. We tuned slab thresholds last quarter, maybe this reg exposed gaps.

sam: Can we confirm by instrumenting the pool to log hits/misses? A minimal patch to print `pool.find(size)` outcomes for the problematic size ranges should be quick. Also add NVTX ranges around pool allocs so traces show hits vs misses.

miguel: I pushed a capture with nvtx tags here: https://artifacts/redwood/perf/1952/nsys-with-nvtx.qdrep. Perf-bot extracted the kernel timeline:```
[1952] pool.hit(size=8192): false
[1952] pool.hit(size=8192): false
[1952] pool.alloc_backend -> cudaMallocAsync (size=8192)
[1952] pool.free(size=8192) -> push_to_slab
```

perf-bot: nsys run finished: /tmp/1952.qdrep. Flamegraph artifact: https://artifacts/redwood/perf/1952/flame.svg :white_check_mark:

jen: Another clue — batching heuristics changed ordering such that we get more interleaved small requests instead of coalesced prefix cache hits. That increases transient working set and stresses the allocator with many concurrent small live buffers.

olivia: Actionable hypothesis: scheduler change altered request ordering, increasing short-lived allocations in a size range not well-covered by current slabs. Fix options: 1) widen slab buckets (add 8k and 16k), 2) make pool.find tolerant (round-up to next slab), 3) revert selector heuristic.

derek: I prefer option 2 + a small slab addition. Option 3 is disruptive to rollout. For quick validation I pushed a branch that rounds allocation sizes up for pool lookup and logs stats: `fix/alloc-roundup-1952`. Patch diff:```diff
- slot = pool.find(size)
+ slot = pool.find(round_up_to_slab(size))
```

sam: Run that branch with the same repro and compare `pool.hit` counts. If hit rate goes from ~12% to >80% we likely avoid the cudaMallocAsync path.

miguel: Ran it already in staging for 30s. Summary:```
before: pool.hit(8k)=0.13, cudaMallocAsync_count=42
after : pool.hit(8k)=0.87, cudaMallocAsync_count=3
95th latency dropped 18%
```

olivia: Nice. Can you attach the new nsys? Also we should add a perf regression test to CI that runs small-batch interleaved scenario for 60s and asserts cudaMallocAsync_count < 10.

miguel: Uploaded: https://artifacts/redwood/perf/1952/roundup-nsys.qdrep. Also added a quick CI job draft in `ci/perf/alloc-smoke.sh`.

jen: We should also check KV cache eviction behavior — if free_to_slab gets delayed, reclaimed buffers might not be available in time. Add NVTX around kvcache->evict paths.

derek: I'll prepare a slab tweak with an additional 8k slab and a 16k bucket and run soak. If combined with roundup it's low risk.

olivia: Plan: (1) land roundup patch behind a flag, dark-launch to staging; (2) add 8k slab bucket; (3) add CI perf smoke; (4) monitor traces + rollback if no improvement. I'll create the rollout ticket and assign owners. :+1:

sam: Thanks. If anyone needs help extracting call stacks from qdrep let me know — I have a small script that maps host stack addresses to symbols even for async allocations.

perf-bot: Bugnote: PERF-1952 created, priority P1, assignees: derek,miguel. Link: https://issues.redwood/PERF-1952

olivia: Great work team. Keep updates in this thread and paste the CI link once green. :rocket:
